strengths: Addresses a relevant and underexplored problem: post-training quantization for DiT-based Real-ISR, and the claim of being the first systematic PTQ framework for this setting appears plausible given the related-work coverage.

The method decomposition is sensible and clearly presented: H-SVD (global low-rank + block-wise rank-1 local branch under a matched parameter budget), VaSMP (data-free, variance-driven cross-layer weight bit allocation derived from standard high-rate quantization distortion analysis), and VaTMP (DP-based temporal activation bit scheduling), each mapped to one of the three identified challenges.

Comprehensive empirical protocol: four real-world benchmarks, comparisons against ten recent PTQ/PEFT baselines under W4A6 and W4A4, ablations for each component, calibration-set robustness checks (Table 8), generalization to a second backbone (DreamClear, Table 7), and an ROI-level artifact analysis (Table 9).

Honest treatment of limitations: the paper acknowledges residual W4A4 artifacts, the mismatch between no-reference IQA metrics and perceptual quality in heavily quantized diffusion SR, the caution needed when interpreting W4A6 > FP scores, and the fact that mixed-precision schedules are currently mapped to standard kernels rather than native arbitrary-precision kernels.

Practical profiling (Tables 5-6) is informative, including the honest note that the 6.14× theoretical operation reduction translates to 4.51× end-to-end speedup due to unquantized components, and that the H-SVD branch costs ~3% latency and slightly more memory than SVDQuant.
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: each component is a relatively direct combination of established techniques — Hadamard rotation and low-rank+residual decomposition follow SVDQuant/QuaRot/RobuQ, temporal bit scheduling follows TDQ, and the variance-based allocation is a closed-form consequence of the standard E[e²] ∝ σ²·2^(-2b) approximation. The main contribution is adaptation to a new task rather than a new mechanism, and the theoretical derivations (Eqs. 12-22) are straightforward applications of known results.

Evaluation reliability is weakened by the authors' own admission: several baselines achieve visibly noisy reconstructions yet score competitively or better on MANIQA (e.g., under W4A4 on DrealSR, Q-Diffusion 0.4991 and EfficientDM 0.4921 vs. 0.4030 for Q-DiT4SR), and the paper concedes a metric-perception mismatch. This substantially undermines unqualified 'SOTA under W4A4' claims; the W4A4 results are mixed rather than dominant (LPIPS degrades from 0.3897 to 0.4327 on DrealSR, and MUSIQ/LIQE are below FP).

The main experiments use a single backbone (DiT4SR); DreamClear (Table 7) is a welcome but thinner generalization check with some metrics below FP even at W4A6 (MUSIQ 62.94 vs 57.77, LIQE 3.472 vs 3.082), which the authors explain via a speculative 'perceptual regularizer' argument rather than direct evidence.

The Gaussianity assumption underlying both the weight quantizer design (Eq. 1-3) and the VaTMP clipping/distortion model (Eqs. 18-20) is asserted and empirically motivated only loosely (KDE plots); no quantitative validation of the distortion model's predictive accuracy against measured quantization error is provided.

Motivating evidence for H-SVD is largely indirect (PCA removal experiments in Fig. 4, output-space projections); there is no analysis of when the block-wise rank-1 branch helps versus hurts, and the rank-budget ablation shows diminishing/negative returns beyond rank 8, suggesting the design space is tuned empirically rather than understood.

Reproducibility is incomplete: the code-release URL is a dangling placeholder ('will be available at'), and key implementation details (block-size search outcomes for SVD-L, exact DP formulation for VaTMP segments, calibration statistics collection procedure under the quantized pipeline) are underspecified.

Some claims are imprecise: the abstract emphasizes 5.8×/6.14× reductions that largely follow from the backbone choice plus mixed precision rather than the proposed components, and Fig. 1 reports identical Params/Ops for SVDQuant and Q-DiT4SR while the text claims advantages from H-SVD's budget-matching, which is confusing without explicit accounting.
